inclusion_rule: Include studies with a decoding pathway that first decodes an explicit articulatory representation (measured or estimated movement trajectories of the articulators, articulatory features or phonological categories) from non-acoustic signals (neural activity, EMG, video, ultrasound, etc.) and then converts it in a next stage to acoustic features, speech waveforms or symbol sequences. Boundary: exclude those whose input itself is an articulatory measurement (EMA, PMA, ultrasound) and that do not decode an articulatory representation as an intermediate. Exclude those that estimate articulation from acoustics and then return to speech (acoustic input). Exclude those that use articulation only as an auxiliary loss or regularization without placing it in the middle of the pathway. Exclude those that only decode an articulatory representation with no next stage. Exclude mentions in reviews or citations only. Count different versions of the same study as one item.
